name: addpipe24_kogge_stone
rationale: Reward is dominated by WNS (10x weight) vs area (0.001x), so the highest-leverage lever is reducing critical-path delay, not area. The frozen best seed (plain '+') already gets mapped to something reasonably fast (WNS 7.52), while our own explicit ripple-carry attempt forced a 24-deep serial carry chain and got much worse WNS (6.16) despite lower area. To push WNS higher without relying on tool-inferred '+' mapping, this candidate implements an explicit 24-bit Kogge-Stone parallel-prefix adder (log2(24)=5 prefix stages instead of 24 serial full-adder stages). This gives a much shallower carry-propagation critical path than the ripple design, and unlike the tested block-partitioned/carry-select masks (12+12, 8+8+8, etc.) which added serialized mux overhead and *hurt* WNS relative to the unsplit '+' baseline, a full-width prefix tree computes all carries in parallel with O(log n) depth and no extra select-mux stage after summation. This is a structurally distinct design from both prior attempts and should plausibly improve or match WNS versus the best-known 530.936-area design, at a modest area cost that is negligible in the reward formula.
